question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=5e{x}^{1/x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5e{x}^{1/x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5e)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{1/x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5e)+(\frac{1}{x})\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5e)+(\frac{1}{x})\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =0+{(\frac{1}{x})}^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+(\frac{1}{x})\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\operatorname{ln}⁡x+(\frac{1}{x})\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & ={x}^{-2}(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y[{x}^{-2}(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=5e{x}^{1/x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =5e{x}^{1/x}[{x}^{-2}(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡x)] \\  & =5e{x}^{1/x-2}\cdot (1-\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$
